facts.football: Rugby league and rugby union (the Raiders and the Brumbies)
facts.water: Lake Burley Griffin, on the Molonglo
facts.founded: 1911, cut from New South Wales for the national capital
facts.origin: Canberra: thought to come from a Ngunnawal word, perhaps "meeting place"

facts.first: The Wreck Bay community, who run Booderee National Park jointly with the government
facts.founded: 1915, given by New South Wales so the capital would have a seaport
facts.origin: Admiral John Jervis (the bay, named in 1791)

facts.first: Wiradjuri, Gamilaraay, Bundjalung, and the Dharug and Eora around Sydney
facts.food: Tim Tams (Arnott's, Sydney) and Hunter Valley wine
facts.climate: Temperate on the coast, semi-arid inland
facts.tz: UTC+10, daylight saving UTC+11 (Broken Hill: UTC+9:30)
facts.founded: 1788, as a penal colony (the First Fleet)
facts.unesco: Sydney Opera House, the Greater Blue Mountains, Lord Howe Island, Willandra Lakes
facts.origin: James Cook thought the coast looked like South Wales (1770)
facts.industry: Finance and services, and coal (the Hunter)

facts.first: Yolngu, Arrernte, Anangu, Warlpiri and the Tiwi; about a third of Territorians are Aboriginal
facts.water: The Katherine River, and Uluru's waterholes
facts.climate: Tropical in the north, desert in the south
facts.founded: 1911, taken from South Australia by the federal government
facts.industry: Gas, mining (uranium, bauxite), tourism and cattle

facts.first: Torres Strait Islanders, Kuku Yalanji, Yidinji, and the Turrbal and Yuggera around Brisbane
facts.water: The Great Artesian Basin, under most of the state
facts.climate: Tropical in the north, subtropical in the south
facts.founded: 1859, split from New South Wales (a penal settlement at Moreton Bay from 1824)
facts.unesco: Great Barrier Reef, the Wet Tropics, K'gari (Fraser Island), Riversleigh fossils

facts.food: Barossa Valley wine and the pie floater
facts.water: The Murray's mouth, and Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre
facts.climate: Mediterranean in the south, desert in the north
facts.founded: 1836, a free settlement: it never took convicts
facts.unesco: Naracoorte Caves and the Flinders Ranges
facts.industry: Wine, copper and uranium (Olympic Dam), and shipbuilding

facts.first: The palawa (Tasmanian Aboriginal people); their revived language is palawa kani
facts.founded: 1825, split from New South Wales as Van Diemen's Land (a penal colony from 1803)
facts.unesco: The Tasmanian Wilderness, Port Arthur and Macquarie Island

facts.first: The Kulin nations (Wurundjeri, Boon wurrung), Gunditjmara and Yorta Yorta
facts.food: Melbourne's coffee, and the Chiko Roll (Bendigo)
facts.football: Australian rules (AFL): it began in Melbourne
facts.wonder: The Twelve Apostles, on the Great Ocean Road
facts.founded: 1851, split from New South Wales (settled freely from 1835)
facts.unesco: Royal Exhibition Building, and the Budj Bim eel traps
facts.plate: Victoria – The Place to Be (once "Garden State")

facts.first: Noongar, Yamatji, Martu and the Wongi
facts.food: Margaret River wine and rock lobster
facts.climate: Mediterranean in the south-west, desert inland, tropical in the north
facts.wonder: Ningaloo Reef and the Bungle Bungles
facts.founded: 1829, as the free Swan River Colony (convicts came later, from 1850)
facts.unesco: Shark Bay, Purnululu, the Ningaloo Coast, Fremantle Prison
facts.plate: Western Australia – The State of Excellence
facts.industry: Iron ore (the Pilbara), gold and gas
